title: Separate repeatable construction from global state and instance isolation
applies_when: A constructor or alias registration changes shared nodes, global names or configuration-class metadata; independent objects may still consult those globals during lookup or serialization.
lesson: Inspect construction and global readers before choosing a repair. Compare repeated and different-option calls with an ordinary control through the real lookup API. Check that creating a second instance does not change the first. Copying constructor data cannot isolate consumers that still read a global table. Serialization may also read a mutable class attribute even when an instance field stays unchanged: compare an earlier object's to_dict and saved JSON after registering another alias. Also save/reload and check a real alias-sensitive consumer: stable canonical metadata can lose the original model type and change dispatch. Before replacing shared classes with alias subclasses, inspect downstream auto mappings: a subclass is not automatically registered just because isinstance still succeeds. In Transformers 5.19, vLLM's DeepseekV3Config is the native HF class recognized by tokenizer and causal-model mappings, while an unregistered differently named child is not. Resolve lifetime, registry identity and pickling contracts before introducing subclasses or removing registration. Confine state loading, file renames and caches to private temporary paths; an in-memory backend does not make the whole constructor side-effect-free.
avoid_when: A one-per-process contract can make independent instances a feature request. A repeated-call failure does not prove a normal one-instance mount fails or a shallow copy is sufficient. Restoring globals after serial tests is isolation, not a concurrent production fix. Distinguish the copied-helper Transformers witness from separately checked full-package get_config on a fixed CPU vLLM wheel; neither qualifies latest-main execution, a repair, serving accuracy or full CI. Missing subclass membership alone is not a failing tokenizer witness: PR62671's exact module overlay passed local WordLevel AutoTokenizer controls on both arms, while fixing the prior-object and fresh-pickle failures. That does not qualify every model/tokenizer mapping or the whole newer package. The JuiceFS sources alone do not establish a supported multi-instance contract. Neither case proves better Scout discovery, PR conversion or cross-framework utility.

evidence.note: NewVFS trims/prefixes global internalNodes, prefixes meta.TrashName, and loads/renames an environment-selected or parent-process-based state file. Source evidence motivates repeat-construction and side-effect controls, not a supported multi-instance contract.
Exported special-name and internal-node lookups consult the shared node table; a constructor-local copy alone cannot provide instance-specific resolution.
Metadata lookup also consumes TrashName. Trace these consumers before treating the VFS node array as the whole ownership boundary.
kimi_k2 and deepseek_v32 map to the same DeepseekV3Config class. _register_config_class changes its model_type before AutoConfig registration. Source mechanism, not full-project validation.

Copied-helper and fixed official e68efc6 CPU full-get_config checks reproduce the mutation. A direct-mapping prototype passed 15 narrow checks but failed six save/reload checks that the original passed; Kimi's real dispatch helper changed selection after alias loss. Prototype rejected. Not latest-main, serving accuracy, an accepted repair or a prospective sample.

Transformers 5.19's AutoModel checks type(config) in its lazy mapping, whose fallback uses registered config class names rather than general subclass inheritance. An offline fixed-wheel CPU probe found native DeepseekV3Config in tokenizer and causal-LM mappings, and a differently named unregistered child in neither. This rejects assuming subclassing is drop-in; it does not test a registered wrapper repair, instantiate a model/tokenizer or prove a serving regression.

Public report of the independently reproduced mixed-alias mutation, stable same-alias control and fixed official CPU environment. It distinguishes historical PR #39554's override-selection contract from prior-object serialization. A submitted report is neither maintainer confirmation nor an accepted repair, latest-main execution or model-output qualification.

Author-owned alias-subclass repair, not our implementation. At head bbde4c4, an independent fixed-e68 CPU one-module overlay passed 15 selected cases versus 11 pass/4 fail for its parent: original alias/override cases plus save/reload, Kimi dispatch, fresh-process pickle, source identity and local WordLevel tokenizer controls. The tokenizer controls pass both arms; missing mapping membership is not itself an actual tokenizer failure. Not a full head build, real model/serving, complete CI or prospective efficacy result.
